title: Model fallback economics and customer migration guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This guide explains the product, economic, and customer-facing approach for model fallback: automatic and policy-driven substitution of a higher-cost, higher-fidelity model with a lower-cost compatible variant when capacity, cost, or SLO constraints make the primary variant undesirable.

Intended audience:
- Product managers owning consumption economics and SLAs
- Engineering teams implementing routing and variant compatibility
- Customer success and sales who coordinate migrations and communications
- Solutions engineers who implement tenant-specific mappings

Goals:
- Define a repeatable economic model to quantify per-request and per-tenant impact when fallback occurs
- Provide a migration and communication playbook to minimize customer surprise and reduce churn
- Specify console/SDK controls and configuration schema for safe rollout and reversible changes
- Establish key observability signals and acceptance thresholds for automated rollback

Background and rationale:
- Customers expect predictable performance and cost. When primary (gold) variants are constrained (capacity, region outage, pricing surge), Redwood can fall back to cheaper or smaller variants (silver/bronze) to preserve availability.
- Fallback preserves request success but can change latency and output characteristics. The platform must: 1) quantify economic delta, 2) surface fidelity changes, and 3) give operators and customers control.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Primary variant (gold): the preferred model variant for a route, has highest fidelity and cost.
- Fallback variants (silver/bronze): degraded-fidelity but compatible variants used when gold is unavailable or undesirable.
- Fallback event: a routing decision where a request is served by a fallback variant.
- Fallback tolerance: per-route or per-tenant policy expressing acceptable frequency and economic exposure to fallbacks.

Economic model (summary):
- Attribution: we attribute the incremental cost delta to a fallback event using token-cost per model variant.
- Delta = cost_gold - cost_fallback. If cost_gold > cost_fallback positive delta indicates immediate savings.
- Customer crediting: when fallback negatively impacts agreed fidelity SLAs, customers receive credit proportional to the expected utility loss (see credit calculator below).

Costing inputs required (console / infra telemetry):
- avg_token_count_per_request (sliding-10m)
- cost_per_token_by_variant (monthly lookup table; USD/token)
- latency_percentiles_by_variant (p50/p95/p99)
- quality_delta_score_by_prompt_set (see evals integration)

Credit calculator (high-level formula):
- economic_savings_per_event = (cost_gold_per_token - cost_fallback_per_token) * avg_token_count_per_request
- fidelity_penalty = max(0, quality_baseline - quality_observed) normalized to [0,1]
- customer_credit_usd = fidelity_penalty * price_multiplier * expected_requests_impacted_in_billing_cycle

Fallback mapping matrix (example):
- The matrix below maps model families and preferred fallbacks. Teams must keep this file in the model catalog and the routing policy.

| Primary family | Preferred fallback | Fallback reason(s)                | Expected latency delta |
|---------------|--------------------|----------------------------------|------------------------|
| redwood-xxl   | redwood-xl-quant   | cost-surge, capacity cap         | +5-15 ms               |
| opt-chat-2.7b | opt-chat-1.3b      | regional outage, preemptible pool| +10-25 ms              |
| open-convo-70b| open-convo-16b-4q  | emergency capacity /burst        | +20-80 ms              |

Policy primitives (per-route or per-tenant):
- fallback_enabled: boolean
- allowed_fallbacks: ordered list of variant ids
- max_fallback_rate: percentage of requests allowed to be served by fallbacks per hour
- credit_on_fallback: enum {none, auto, manual-review}
- notify_on_first_fallback: boolean

Configuration schema (console/SDK example):
- The platform exposes a JSON route policy. Example (stringified here):

"{\n  \"route_id\": \"billing-summary-v1\",\n  \"fallback_policy\": {\n    \"enabled\": true,\n    \"allowed_fallbacks\": [\"redwood-xl-quant\", \"redwood-l-quant\"],\n    \"max_fallback_rate\": 0.05,\n    \"credit_on_fallback\": \"auto\",\n    \"notify_on_first_fallback\": true\n  }\n}"

Rollout and customer migration playbook (operational steps):
1) Preparation (2–4 weeks before run):
   - Run cross-variant evals on representative prompt sets (customer-provided and internal) and record quality_delta_score_by_prompt_set.
   - Compute expected economic impact using the cost model and the customer’s recent token profile.
   - Identify customers with low fallback tolerance (customer tier + contractual SLOs).
2) Canary (1 week):
   - Enable fallback for a small percentage of traffic (max_fallback_rate=0.01) for internal tenants and select friendly customers.
   - Observe: fallback_rate, per-tenant latency p95, quality_regressions (automated eval probes).
   - If fidelity_penalty > threshold (0.12) or latency p95 increases > 30%, pause rollouts and open a triage.
3) Gradual expansion (2–6 weeks):
   - Incrementally raise max_fallback_rate by doubling interval while monitoring metrics and conducting weekly sync with CS.
   - Send proactive communications to impacted customers with clear mitigation options (pin gold variant, opt-out).
4) Customer migration (when deprecating a gold variant):
   - Provide a migration window (90 days recommended) with automated migration helper that suggests the nearest fallback + estimated cost/quality delta.
   - Offer tools to pin model version and to schedule a controlled switch (canary + rollback hooks).
5) Post-migration review (30 days after complete switch):
   - Run per-customer quality audits and reconcile any credits applied.

Customer communication templates (short):
- First fallback notification (automated): "On YYYY-MM-DD your route X experienced a temporary fallback to redwood-xl-quant due to capacity constraints. No requests failed; some responses may be lower fidelity. If you require strict fidelity, pin the gold variant in the Console."
- Migration plan offer (CS template): "We recommend a 30–90 day migration window; we will run your prompt set against recommended fallbacks and deliver an impact report. We can also schedule a partner-migration run where Redwood engineers support tuning prompts."

Console and API changes required:
- Route policy editor: add fallback primitives and show simulated economic impact for the customer based on recent token usage.
- Alerts: automatic alert to CS when individual customer fallback_rate > 5% for 1 hour.
- Billing integration: track fallback events as distinct line items for reporting and potential credits.

Observability and SLOs (operational thresholds):
- Primary SLOs to track:
  - fallback_rate (global and per-tenant): target <= 0.5% long-term; alert at 5%/1h
  - avg_quality_delta (per-prompt-set): target <= 0.05; alert at 0.12
  - latency_p95_delta_by_variant: target <= 25% relative increase
- Dashboards to build:
  - Fallback heatmap (region x time x variant)
  - Per-tenant fallback ledger (events, credits, manual overrides)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customer surprise leading to churn. Mitigation: mandatory first-fallback notification + CS outreach for tiered customers.
- Risk: over-crediting erodes revenue. Mitigation: tie credits to measurable quality regressions and require manual approval for large credits.
- Risk: model incompatibility yields incorrect structured outputs. Mitigation: compatibility tests and explicit contract checks for structured-output routes.

Ownership and success metrics:
- Owner: Product (economics) / Eng Routing (implementation) / CS (customer ops)
- Quarterly KPIs:
  - % of routes with fallback_policy defined (target 95% coverage for high-volume routes)
  - Reduction of outage-induced errors by fallback mechanism (target 80% fewer failed requests in constrained events)
  - Net revenue impact from fallback credits (target < 0.5% of ARR)
  - Customer satisfaction post-migration (CSAT >= 4.2)

Appendix A — Example evaluation checklist for candidate fallbacks:
- Verify prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds (acceptance thresholds defined per use-case).
- Structural contract tests for JSON/SQL/Function outputs pass 100% for critical routes.
- Latency p95 within acceptable band for interactive products.

Appendix B — Example audit record format (CSV-friendly):
- timestamp,route_id,tenant_id,primary_variant,fallback_variant,reason,token_count,latency_ms,quality_delta,credit_applied_usd

Operational notes and next steps (for roadmap):
- Q4 2026: integrate evals automation into canary pipeline to provide per-canary quality_delta in near real-time.
- Q1 2027: console feature to simulate cost/quality tradeoffs for arbitrary fallback chains.
- Ongoing: tighten crediting formula in partnership with Finance to reduce edge-case exposure.

If you implement changes based on this guide, add a short changelog entry to the route policy and notify the CS playbook channel.
